experiment: paper_swap final1 - cross-stack retarget of the adiabatic 1x2 mode-evolution splitter
spec: transmission_total >= 0.95 AND split_balance = 0.5 +/- 0.02, at 1550nm fundamental TE
measured_by: conductor FDTD (tier-1), capped at 3 calls/stack; agent is the optimizer (tier-0 mode solves)

soi220.note: Best is round-1 (tight merged-regime coupling). The gap-opening unmerge fix that CLOSED sin400 REGRESSED soi220 on both axes (T 0.928->0.880, balance ->0.4638): strong confinement prefers the tighter coupling. 0.022 short of spec.

sin400.note: Flagged-risk stack, closed on round 2. Round-1 diagnosis (merged Y-junction pinch-tip radiation) fixed by opening the constant gap mf/2 -> mf (unmerged evanescent coupler, 6.2x adiabatic) + C1 sine fan-out.

tfln400.note: Gap trend saturated at T~0.93. Floor: the 0.5um min_feature pinch tip radiates; a clean un-merge (gap=mf=0.5) needs Lc=64um -> ~200um device > 150um budget. >=0.95 not reachable for TFLN within budget.

cross_cutting_findings: Split balance is structurally exact (0.500-0.5075) on ALL stacks: mirror symmetry -> even supermode -> 50/50, independent of platform. Transmission was the entire fight.

Dominant loss was NOT transfer adiabaticity (all designs were 4-13x adiabatic) but the center pinch-off tip radiating in the merged-gap regime; opening the gap to min_feature is the cure where the budget allows it.
Retargeting is regime-dependent, not one-size-fits-all: the same unmerge move closed SiN (weak confinement) but regressed SOI (strong confinement).
TFLN's min_feature (0.5um) sets a hard within-budget transmission floor (~0.93) for this Y-junction-regime splitter.
